summary: Dedicated pool throughput degradation correlated with long-lived multiplexed connections from customer sidecar
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (AtlasData, dedicated) reports sustained p99 latency increases and per-second throughput drops in their reserved GPU pool starting 2026-03-08 14:10 UTC. Symptoms coincide with a large number of long-lived multiplexed websocket/concurrent keepalive connections from the customer's sidecar process. Impact: production traffic experiences ~20-40% throughput degradation and elevated token latency for batched routes.

Impact:
- Customer-visible increased p99 generation latency (from ~230ms to ~680ms) and reduced overall RPCs/sec served by the reserved pool.
- Several auto-failovers to lower-tier model variants observed after autoscaler throttled new attachments.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: atlas-dedicated-us-east-1-001
- Region: us-east-1
- Production traffic, customer on dedicated plan with 8 GPUs reserved

Steps to reproduce (customer reproduction):
1) Deploy sidecar v2.14.3 with multiplex enabled and keepalive interval 15s.
2) Open 2k concurrent long-lived websocket connections streaming occasional short inference requests.
3) Observe allocator attach rate and autoscaler decisions over ~10 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Many active connections remain idle for long stretches but hold attachments in the scheduler layer.
- Autoscaler sees apparent demand (connections + small requests) and triggers scaled provisioning, but GPU slot attach+warmup fails to convert into efficient batched throughput, causing slot fragmentation and transient shortages.
- Serving runtime reports higher NVLink contention and more frequent small-batch kernels which exacerbate p99.

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived multiplexed connections should not reserve or block GPU attachments when idle; the scheduler/allocator should cap warmup and prefer burstable pooling to preserve throughput for active batches.

Logs / Metrics / Observability pointers:
- Grafana: dashboard "dedicated/atlas-dedicated-us-east-1-001" panels: attach_rate, slot_utilization, nvlink_io_wait, allocator_queue_depth (see spikes 2026-03-08 14:08-14:30 UTC).
- Traces: sample trace IDs: trace-20260308-14-12-7a9c, trace-20260308-14-20-b3f1 (high attach latency + fallback).
- Customer-provided logs: sidecar_connect.log (attached in ticket) shows thousands of keepalive frames with intermittent short RPCs.

Attachments:
- sidecar_connect.log (customer)
- perf-grafana-snapshot-2026-03-08.png

Business impact:
- Customer reports feature degradation in their product during US business hours; revenue-sensitive.
comments: 2026-03-09 09:22 - Sara Kim (Support): Initial triage done; validated customer metrics and escalated to SRE. Assigned to Marcus.

2026-03-09 11:05 - Marcus Rivera (SRE): Observed allocator_queue_depth spikes matching customer's timeline. Hypothesis: long-lived multiplexed connections are being treated as active demand and preventing efficient batching. Starting deeper heap/profile capture on pool.

2026-03-09 13:41 - Marcus Rivera (SRE): Collected kernel activity. NVLink stalls correlate with many small kernel launches from mixed model variants. Reproduced locally with a sidecar load generator; confirmed increased small-batch kernel fraction.

2026-03-09 16:03 - Eugene Park (Backend Eng): Reviewed autoscaler logs. Autoscaler warmup heuristics triggered additional capacity then retracted due to low steady throughput, causing churn. Suggest limiting warmup attach when connection churn is high.

2026-03-10 08:14 - Support (Sara Kim): Shared temporary mitigation with customer: reduce sidecar keepalive concurrency and enable request coalescing in the SDK. Customer to test during afternoon window.

2026-03-10 17:22 - AtlasData (Customer): Confirmed immediate improvement after reducing concurrent connections by 60%. Throughput returned within 10% of baseline. Asking for long-term fix to avoid manual tuning.

2026-03-11 10:35 - Marcus Rivera (SRE): Deployed autoscaler patch (hotfix) to 1) cap warmup attaches per-pool 2) add idle-attachment timeout for multiplexed connections. Patch rolled to canary and two dedicated pools overnight.

2026-03-12 09:00 - Eugene Park (Backend Eng): Monitoring post-fix metrics; initial results promising. Need to add baked telemetry to detect similar patterns and a runbook for customer-facing guidance.
investigation_notes: Heap/profile captures show many scheduler handles in "wait_for_attach" state while connections idle - suggests attachments are being reserved earlier than necessary.
Autoscaler warmup heuristic (warmup_attach_goal) was set high for this pool due to historical burst patterns; warmup reconfiguration required to be connection-aware.
Small-batch kernel fraction rose from 12% baseline to 48% during event window, increasing per-token latency due to kernel launch overhead and NVLink contention.
Reproduction locally with sidecar emulator confirmed that toggling multiplex off restored efficient batching and slot consolidation.
No evidence of driver-level GPU faults; this is a scheduling/heuristic interaction between sidecar behavior, scheduler attachment, and autoscaler warmup policies.
resolution: Rolled a short-lived hotfix to the autoscaler (2026-03-11 02:00 UTC) that: 1) limits concurrent warmup attaches per dedicated pool, 2) introduces an idle-attachment TTL for multiplexed connections so idle sockets don't reserve attachments, 3) lowers the warmup_attach_goal for pools with high connection churn. Customer applied SDK-side temporary mitigation (reduced concurrency + request coalescing). Post-fix monitoring shows throughput returned to within 95% of baseline and p99 latency improved. No further GPU OOMs or driver errors were observed.
follow_up_actions: Create a formal runbook documenting detection and mitigation steps for long-lived multiplexed-connection induced degradation (owner: SRE).
Add telemetry: metric 'multiplex_idle_attachment_count' and alert when ratio to active_attachments > 0.25 (owner: Observability).
Make autoscaler warmup heuristics connection-aware in next sprint (ENG-allocator team; linked PR created).
Customer-facing guidance: update Dedicated onboarding docs with recommended sidecar defaults for multiplexing (support + docs).
Postmortem to be drafted if any regression repeats in the next 30 days (owner: Incident Lead).
